sections.title: Shrub and flowers
sections.text: The Mauritian boucle d’oreille is an endemic shrub about 2–3 m tall, with striking reddish-orange, bell-shaped flowers. It blooms mainly from June to October. The plate’s red pendant bells and oval leaves match the plant.

sections.title: Name and range
sections.text: Kew currently accepts this species as Ruizia boutoniana and lists Trochetia boutoniana as a synonym. It is native to Mauritius; the government identifies it as the national flower, declared in 1992. No edible use is established by these sources.
